q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a steel door?
title: Steel door carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the steel sheet and frame in one door, including cutting scrap, and apply your steel supplier's factor. Add infill such as honeycomb paper or rockwool, powder coating and oven fuel, welding and press electricity, hardware and packing. Divide by doors dispatched. Steel is usually most of the total.

ul: Galvanised or cold rolled sheet for leaves and frames.
Infill: honeycomb paper, PU foam or mineral wool for fire doors.
Hinges, locks, vision glass and gaskets.
Shearing, punching, press brake and welding electricity.
Pretreatment and powder coating, with oven LPG, PNG or electricity.

p: Report each size and type separately: a fire-rated door carries more steel and infill than a standard one.

example.title: Worked example: steel door plant per door (one month)
lines: Powder oven PNG: 3,000 SCM x 2.05 = 6,150 kg CO2
Plant total: 23,900 / 1,500 = 15.93 kg CO2 per door
Add sheet steel, infill and hardware for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
